hero.headline: U.S. Strikes Iran Military Sites for Second Time in Three Days
hero.body:
The United States carried out new strikes on military targets in southern Iran, marking the second such attack within three days. A U.S. official said the strikes were conducted in self-defense.

The targets included four one-way attack drones and a drone ground-control station, according to the official. The strikes were carried out as efforts to negotiate a cease-fire continue.

The attacks come during what officials describe as a fragile cease-fire between the United States and Iran. The two countries have been engaged in negotiations aimed at ending a conflict that has lasted three months.

The renewed military action raises questions about the durability of the current cease-fire arrangement. U.S. officials characterized the strikes as defensive measures in response to active threats.

The conflict has now extended beyond direct confrontation between the United States and Iran. Israel has intensified its operations in southern Lebanon, where clashes with Hezbollah have increased in recent days.

In Lebanon, residents have expressed doubt that diplomatic efforts will bring lasting peace to their country, even if negotiators reach an agreement to end the broader war. The fighting between Israel and Hezbollah continues to escalate in the southern part of the country.

The strikes have already affected global markets. Oil prices rose following the attacks, driven by renewed concerns about potential disruptions to shipping traffic through the Strait of Hormuz, a critical waterway for global oil supplies.

Iran had imposed a near-total internet shutdown lasting 88 days during the conflict. The government has recently begun allowing some people to reconnect with the outside world, though access remains limited and uncertain.

President Trump said Iran is "negotiating on fumes" and stated he feels no political pressure to reach a deal before upcoming midterm elections. He indicated willingness to continue the current approach rather than rush to an agreement.

The timing of the strikes, coming as cease-fire negotiations remain active, highlights the precarious nature of current diplomatic efforts. Both sides continue military operations while simultaneously pursuing talks to end the conflict.

cards.headline: US military strikes Iranian drone site amid ongoing peace negotiations
cards.body:
The US military shot down four Iranian attack drones and struck a ground control station in Bandar Abbas that was preparing to launch a fifth drone, a US official said Wednesday. The incident occurred in the Strait of Hormuz when Iranian forces targeted a commercial ship with one-way attack drones.

US Central Command confirmed its forces intercepted the drones that posed a threat in the strait. Bandar Abbas is a port city on Iran's southern coast. A senior US official characterized this as the second such clash in 48 hours.

The military action took place as the US and Iran are engaged in negotiations to end their ongoing conflict. President Donald Trump addressed the situation during a Cabinet meeting Wednesday, though his remarks differed from weekend statements suggesting an agreement was near. Trump maintained what officials described as maximum demands on Iran during the talks.

The strikes represent a continuation of military tensions even as diplomatic efforts proceed. The US attacked the Iranian drone-launching unit on the ground before it could deploy additional weapons, according to the senior official who spoke on condition of anonymity.

The Strait of Hormuz serves as a critical waterway for global shipping and energy transport. Iranian drone attacks on commercial vessels in the area have occurred repeatedly during the broader conflict between the two nations. US forces maintain a regular presence in the region to protect shipping lanes and respond to threats against civilian maritime traffic.

Neither government has provided details about the substance of ongoing peace negotiations or a timeline for potential agreement. The continued military exchanges raise questions about the progress of diplomatic talks aimed at resolving the conflict.

cards.headline: Uganda Closes Border With Congo as Ebola Cases Rise
cards.teaser: Uganda has closed its border with the Democratic Republic of Congo after seven confirmed Ebola cases appeared in the capital.
cards.body:
Uganda shut its border with the Democratic Republic of Congo as Ebola cases continue to surge in the region. Seven confirmed cases of the virus have been reported in Kampala, Uganda's capital city.

The outbreak in the DRC has grown significantly, with authorities reporting over 900 suspected cases and 119 suspected deaths. The WHO has characterized the situation as posing a "very high" risk for the country, though the risk of global spread remains low. Ugandan officials have activated disease surveillance systems to monitor and respond to the outbreak, while neighboring countries have implemented containment measures.

cards.headline: FBI arrests former CIA official with $40 million in gold bars at home
cards.teaser: Federal prosecutors charged a former CIA officer with stealing 300 gold bars from the agency.
cards.body:
The FBI arrested David Rush, a former CIA official, after discovering approximately $40 million worth of gold bars in his home. Prosecutors allege Rush stole roughly 300 gold bars from the agency.

Federal agents also seized cash and multiple Rolex watches during the arrest. Rush allegedly faked being a Navy pilot as part of a broader pattern of deception, according to prosecutors. The case represents one of the largest alleged thefts from a US intelligence agency in recent history.

cards.headline: Washington paper mill disaster may be state's deadliest industrial accident
cards.teaser: Eleven workers are presumed dead after an implosion at a Longview paper mill.
cards.body:
A tank ruptured at Nippon Dynawave Packaging Co in Longview, Washington on Tuesday morning, killing at least two workers. Nine others remain missing and presumed dead following the incident at the paper mill facility.

The governor of Washington has characterized the disaster as potentially the deadliest industrial tragedy in the state's modern history. Nine additional workers were injured in the incident. Authorities are continuing recovery operations for the missing workers.

cards.headline: Justice Department opens investigation into Trump accuser E. Jean Carroll
cards.teaser: The DOJ has launched a criminal investigation into E. Jean Carroll focusing on possible perjury in her deposition testimony.
cards.body:
The Trump administration has opened a criminal investigation into E. Jean Carroll, the writer who accused President Trump of sexual assault. According to reports from CNN and the New York Times, prosecutors are examining whether Carroll committed perjury during a 2022 deposition tied to her civil lawsuits against Trump.

The investigation focuses on statements Carroll made under oath about whether she received outside financial support for her legal battles. Carroll previously won civil verdicts against Trump in cases involving defamation and sexual assault allegations.

cards.headline: Record Heat Wave Breaks Temperature Records Across Western Europe
cards.teaser: An early season heat wave has shattered temperature records in multiple European capitals including London, Paris, and Madrid.
cards.body:
Western Europe is gripped by an exceptionally early heat wave that has shattered temperature records across multiple countries. London has reached 95 degrees for consecutive days, while Paris and other major capitals are experiencing punishingly hot conditions well above typical May averages. Government warnings have been issued as the extreme heat poses serious health risks to residents.

Experts warn that unpredictable and extreme weather patterns are becoming increasingly frequent. The buckled jet stream pattern driving this heat wave is the same atmospheric condition contributing to turbulent weather in other regions like California. As temperatures continue to climb across the continent, the crisis underscores growing concerns about climate-related weather volatility.

cards.headline: DOJ charges Google employee over insider trading on prediction market
cards.teaser: A Google staffer allegedly used insider information to profit $1.2 million on Polymarket.
cards.body:
The Department of Justice has charged a Google engineer with insider trading after he allegedly used confidential information about Google's 2025 Year in Search campaign to place bets on Polymarket, a prediction market platform. The engineer risked over $2.7 million in wagers and made approximately $1.2 million in profits from the trades.

This marks the second known federal criminal case involving insider trading on a prediction market platform. The charges reflect growing government attention to potential securities violations on prediction markets, which have expanded in popularity but remain largely unregulated.

cards.headline: Google engineer charged with insider trading after making $1.2 million on Polymarket
cards.body:
Federal prosecutors in New York charged a longtime Google employee with insider trading after he allegedly used confidential company information to make $1.2 million in bets on Polymarket, a prediction market platform.

The engineer worked at Google and allegedly accessed internal data that gave him an advantage when placing bets on the platform. Prosecutors say he violated insider trading laws by using this non-public information for personal financial gain.

Polymarket allows users to bet on the outcomes of future events, from political elections to economic indicators. The platform has grown in popularity as a way to gauge public sentiment on various topics, but it has also attracted scrutiny over potential manipulation and misuse.

The case marks a notable application of insider trading law beyond traditional stock markets. While insider trading typically involves securities like stocks and bonds, prosecutors are applying similar legal principles to prediction markets where information asymmetry can create unfair advantages.

The charges did not specify what type of internal Google data the employee allegedly accessed or how that information translated into profitable bets on Polymarket. The engineer's position at Google and the duration of the alleged trading activity were also not detailed in available information about the charges.

Google has not publicly commented on the charges against its employee. The company maintains strict policies around the use of confidential information and regularly trains employees on legal and ethical obligations regarding proprietary data.

The case could set precedent for how insider trading laws apply to emerging financial platforms and prediction markets. Legal experts have debated whether traditional securities laws should extend to betting platforms, particularly as these markets grow in size and influence.

If convicted, the engineer could face significant fines and potential prison time. Federal insider trading charges typically carry maximum sentences of 20 years in prison, though actual sentences vary widely based on the specifics of each case and cooperation with authorities.

cards.headline: Court orders customs chief to address tariff refund compliance
cards.teaser: A judge demanded the official appear at a hearing about efforts to repay $166 billion in illegally imposed tariffs.
cards.body:
A federal court ordered the head of US Customs to appear at a hearing to address compliance with tariff refund requirements. The demand signals judicial concern about the Trump administration's progress in repaying $166 billion owed from tariffs that were ruled illegal.

The court's decision to require personal appearance by the customs chief represents an escalation in oversight of the refund process. The substantial sum stems from tariffs previously determined to have been imposed without proper legal authority.

cards.headline: Australia sues 3M for $2 billion over contamination from firefighting foam
cards.teaser: The Australian government has filed a lawsuit against 3M seeking $2 billion in damages over contamination caused by PFAS chemicals.
cards.body:
Australia's government has launched what it calls its largest ever lawsuit, seeking $2 billion in damages from 3M over PFAS contamination at 28 defence bases. The American manufacturing company produced firefighting foam containing PFAS chemicals, known as "forever chemicals" because they persist indefinitely in the environment and human bodies.

The contamination stems from decades of using the foam for firefighting training and emergency response at Australian defence facilities. The government is pursuing the case to recover costs associated with addressing the widespread contamination across the affected sites.

cards.headline: California court rejects Tesla's bid to dismiss racial discrimination lawsuit
cards.teaser: A California court has denied Tesla's attempt to throw out a racial discrimination lawsuit, clearing the way for a trial in July.
cards.body: A California court has rejected Tesla's motion to dismiss a racial discrimination lawsuit before trial. The state's civil rights agency, which brought the case, called the ruling a victory and said it expects to proceed to trial in July. The lawsuit alleges racial discrimination at Tesla facilities, and the agency will now present its case against the electric vehicle manufacturer in court.

cards.headline: Hurricanes Take Commanding 3-1 Lead in Eastern Conference Finals
cards.body:
The Carolina Hurricanes moved within one win of reaching the Stanley Cup Final after defeating the Montreal Canadiens in Game 4 of the Eastern Conference finals. Goaltender Frederik Andersen recorded a shutout with 18 saves, his third of the postseason through 12 playoff games this year.

The Hurricanes dominated in Montreal, building a 3-1 series lead over the Canadiens. Andersen turned away every shot he faced to secure the victory on the road. The win puts Carolina in position to close out the series in Game 5, scheduled for Friday.

The shutout performance marked Andersen's third clean sheet of these playoffs, demonstrating the veteran goaltender's consistency in high-pressure situations. His 18-save night was part of a comprehensive team effort that saw the Hurricanes control play throughout the game.

Carolina now has three opportunities to advance to the Stanley Cup Final, starting with Game 5. The Hurricanes have outscored and outplayed Montreal through four games of the series, establishing themselves as the clear favorites to represent the Eastern Conference in the championship round.

The Canadiens face elimination as they prepare to host Game 5 on Friday. Montreal will need to win three consecutive games to overturn the series deficit and advance to the Final. The team has struggled to generate offense against Andersen and the Hurricanes' defensive structure throughout the conference finals.

If Carolina completes the series win, they will await the winner of the Western Conference finals for a chance at the franchise's second Stanley Cup championship. The Hurricanes' playoff run has been built on strong goaltending and balanced scoring, elements that were on full display in their Game 4 victory.

cards.headline: Former judges ask court to reopen Trump IRS settlement case
cards.teaser: A bipartisan group of former federal judges challenged the Trump administration's settlement that created a $1.776 billion fund.
cards.body:
A group of former federal judges asked a federal court Wednesday to reopen President Trump's lawsuit against the Internal Revenue Service. The judges argued that the administration circumvented the court by negotiating a settlement with the president directly.

The settlement created a $1.776 billion fund for people who believe the government has wronged them. The bipartisan group of former judges contends this arrangement bypassed proper judicial oversight of the case.

cards.headline: Iran Restores Limited Internet Access After 88-Day Shutdown
cards.teaser: The Iranian government has begun allowing some citizens to reconnect to the internet after imposing a near-total shutdown for nearly three months.
cards.body:
Iran is letting people connect with the outside world again after an 88-day period of heavily censored news, television, and internet access. The government imposed the near-total internet shutdown during the recent conflict with the United States.

Access remains uneven across the country. Those who have regained connectivity are uncertain about how long the restored access will continue.

cards.headline: Lebanon Expects Prolonged Conflict Despite U.S.-Iran Negotiations
cards.teaser: Lebanese residents say they do not believe diplomatic efforts will bring peace as fighting between Israel and Hezbollah intensifies.
cards.body:
Few people in Lebanon believe that current diplomatic efforts to end the wider war will bring peace to their country. Clashes between Israel and Hezbollah have intensified in southern Lebanon in recent days.

The pessimism persists even as the United States and Iran engage in negotiations aimed at ending the three-month conflict. Lebanese citizens remain resigned to a prolonged period of warfare regardless of any agreement reached between the primary combatants.

cards.headline: Trump administration in talks to fund US drone companies
cards.teaser: The administration is discussing financial support for domestic drone manufacturers.
cards.body: The Trump administration has entered into discussions about providing funding to US drone companies. The talks represent a potential shift in government support for the domestic drone manufacturing industry.

cards.headline: Ferrari's first electric car faces criticism from investors and analysts
cards.teaser: The new model sparked memes, analyst skepticism, and a stock selloff following its reveal.
cards.body:
Ferrari's new Luce electric vehicle has sparked significant backlash following its unveiling. Social media users mocked the model, while analysts questioned its market viability. The negative reception prompted investors to sell shares in the Italian automaker.

A former Ferrari chairman expressed concerns that the shift to electric vehicles could damage the company's storied legacy. The divided public response highlights challenges Ferrari faces as it navigates the transition away from traditional combustion engines amid competition from Chinese EV makers.

cards.headline: Rivian sets June 9 for first R2 SUV deliveries
cards.teaser: Rivian will deliver its first R2 SUVs to customers on June 9, the company announced.
cards.body:
Rivian has announced June 9 as the date for first customer deliveries of the R2 SUV. CEO RJ Scaringe has described the vehicle as "maybe the most important thing we've launched to date," underscoring its significance to the company's future.

The R2 marks an important expansion of Rivian's product lineup beyond its initial R1T truck and R1S SUV models.

cards.headline: Researchers achieve perfectly random number generation using quantum chips
cards.teaser: Scientists have created certifiably perfect randomness for the first time using entangled quantum computing chips.
cards.body:
The experimental randomness amplification was achieved through quantum entanglement between chips. True randomness has applications in cryptography and data security, where unpredictable numbers are essential for protecting information.

The quantum computing system's ability to generate perfect randomness could help keep secrets safe by making encryption keys impossible to predict. Previous random number generators relied on methods that could theoretically be compromised or predicted with enough computing power.

cards.headline: Georgia Coach Suggests SEC Could Leave NCAA Over Playoff Disagreements
cards.teaser: Kirby Smart commented that the SEC might essentially secede if an agreement cannot be reached on College Football Playoff matters.
cards.body:
Georgia head coach Kirby Smart indicated during college football spring meetings that the SEC could leave the NCAA if no agreement is reached on playoff format issues. His comments about the conference potentially seceding have raised significant questions about the future direction of college football governance.

Conference expansion has been a major focus of the spring meetings. Smart's remarks represent an escalation in ongoing discussions about playoff structures and the SEC's role within the current NCAA framework.

cards.headline: Phillies Pitcher Cristopher Sanchez Sets Franchise Record With Scoreless Streak
cards.teaser: Cristopher Sanchez extended his scoreless innings streak to 44 innings, surpassing a Phillies franchise record set by Hall of Famer Grover Cleveland Alexander in 1911.
cards.body:
Phillies pitcher Cristopher Sánchez set a new franchise record on Wednesday, extending his scoreless innings streak to 44⅔ innings. He surpassed the previous mark held by Hall of Famer Grover Cleveland Alexander, whose record had stood since 1911.

Sánchez's achievement represents the longest scoreless streak in Philadelphia Phillies history, breaking a record that had lasted over a century.

cards.headline: Horror Film Obsession Breaks Box Office Record With Second-Weekend Spike
cards.body:
The horror film Obsession has made box office history by increasing its earnings in its second weekend, a pattern not seen since Sound of Freedom. The film has become what industry observers are calling this summer's breakout box office hit.

The second-weekend spike marks an unusual achievement in theatrical releases, where films typically see declining revenues after their opening weekend. The performance has drawn comparisons to Sound of Freedom, which similarly saw audience growth after its initial release.

Industry tracking shows the film's momentum continuing beyond typical horror movie patterns. The success has established Obsession as a record-breaking entry in the horror genre, though specific box office figures were not disclosed in initial reports.

The film's photography has also drawn attention from industry publications, with critics highlighting its visual approach. The combination of strong word-of-mouth and repeat viewings appears to be driving the continued box office performance.

Obsession's trajectory differs from standard horror releases, which often front-load their earnings during opening weekend before sharp declines. The sustained audience interest suggests the film is reaching beyond typical horror demographics.

The achievement comes during a competitive summer movie season. While many releases see diminishing returns after their debuts, Obsession has bucked industry trends with measurable growth in its second frame.

Distribution analysts are watching whether the film can maintain momentum into subsequent weekends. The second-weekend increase has already secured its place in box office history, joining Sound of Freedom as one of the rare films to achieve this pattern in recent years.

The success represents a significant win for the horror genre, which has produced several breakout hits in recent years but rarely with this specific pattern of sustained growth after opening weekend.

cards.headline: Appeals court allows Palestinian activist to remain free pending Supreme Court appeal
cards.teaser: A federal appeals panel ruled that Mahmoud Khalil can stay out of custody while petitioning the Supreme Court.
cards.body:
A federal appeals court panel ruled Tuesday that pro-Palestinian activist Mahmoud Khalil may remain free while he appeals his case against the Trump administration to the Supreme Court. The three-judge panel included judges appointed by Presidents Trump, George W. Bush, and Joe Biden.

Judges Stephanos Bibas, Arianna Freeman, and Thomas Hardiman issued the decision, allowing Khalil to proceed with his legal challenge while the case moves forward in the Supreme Court.

cards.headline: Jill Biden Says She Feared Husband Was Having Stroke During 2024 Debate
cards.teaser: The former first lady told CBS News she was frightened by President Biden's performance against Donald Trump.
cards.body:
Jill Biden told CBS News that she was frightened by Joe Biden's performance during the 2024 presidential debate against Donald Trump. The former first lady said she thought her husband might have suffered a stroke while watching his faltering debate performance.

"I was frightened, because I had never, ever seen Joe like that before or since. Never," Biden said in an interview set to air on Sunday. Her comments offer an intimate perspective on a pivotal moment that significantly impacted the 2024 presidential campaign.

cards.headline: Republicans reconcile with Ken Paxton after contentious Texas Senate primary
cards.teaser: Party leaders are breaking the ice with Paxton following a brutal primary campaign.
cards.body:
Republican leaders are moving to rebuild relationships with Ken Paxton following a bruising Texas Senate primary. The race created significant divisions within the party, but officials are now working to unify behind Paxton as he prepares for the general election matchup.

Democrat James Talarico is pivoting his strategy for the general election, shifting away from his primary message to attack Paxton's past scandals. Political analysts are evaluating whether Democrats can overcome Texas's long history of favoring Republican candidates in statewide races.

cards.headline: FIFA investigated over World Cup ticket pricing practices
cards.teaser: New York and New Jersey are examining whether fans were misled about ticket sales and seating.
cards.body:
The attorneys general of New York and New Jersey have launched an investigation into FIFA's ticket sales and pricing practices. The probe was triggered by reports that fans were misled about ticket availability and seat locations for World Cup matches.

FIFA has been ordered to provide explanations regarding its ticketing approach for the 2026 World Cup. The investigation examines whether the organization gave accurate information to ticket purchasers.

cards.headline: NASA spacecraft captures detailed Mars images during flyby
cards.teaser: A NASA spacecraft has sent back high-resolution images of Mars, including views of the south pole, during a recent flyby.
cards.body:
The Psyche spacecraft captured spectacular views of Mars as it passed by the red planet on its journey to study a distant asteroid. The images include high-resolution photographs of the Martian south pole.

The Mars flyby was not Psyche's primary mission objective. Instead, the spacecraft is traveling to examine a metal-rich asteroid in the asteroid belt, making these images a bonus scientific opportunity during its voyage through the inner solar system.

cards.headline: SEC Commissioner Defends Conference Despite Big Ten Playoff Dominance
cards.teaser: Greg Sankey said the SEC still 'stands alone' despite the Big Ten winning the past three national titles and holding a 4-0 record against the SEC in recent College Football Playoff matchups.
cards.body:
SEC Commissioner Greg Sankey declared his conference still stands alone as the nation's best, despite the Big Ten's recent dominance. The Big Ten has won three consecutive national championships and maintains a perfect 4-0 record against the SEC in head-to-head College Football Playoff matchups over the past three seasons.

Despite the stark on-field evidence favoring the Big Ten, Sankey maintained confidence in the SEC's overall strength and continued relevance in college football's power structure.

cards.headline: Arizona Forward Koa Peat Stays in NBA Draft
cards.teaser: Koa Peat, a projected first-round pick, is keeping his name in the NBA draft after playing forward for Arizona.
cards.body:
Arizona forward Koa Peat has decided to keep his name in the NBA draft, sources told ESPN on Wednesday. Peat is projected to be selected in the first round.

The decision means the forward will forgo returning to college basketball and instead pursue his professional career in the NBA.

cards.headline: Former Super Bowl MVP Von Miller Lobbies Broncos for Return
cards.teaser: Von Miller said he is playing for somebody in the 2026 season and has already asked Denver coach Sean Payton to sign him.
cards.body:
Former Super Bowl MVP Von Miller has made it clear he will play in the 2026 season. In recent comments, Miller said he is "for sure" suiting up for somebody next year and has already reached out to Denver Broncos head coach Sean Payton about a potential return.

Miller, who previously won a Super Bowl with the Broncos, is lobbying the franchise to bring him back. The overture to Payton represents Miller's direct pitch to reunite with his former team.

cards.headline: ABC News and National Geographic Win Big at News Emmy Awards
cards.teaser: ABC News took eight awards including the top prize for outstanding live news program at the 47th annual News Emmys.
cards.body:
ABC World News Tonight With David Muir won the outstanding live news program category for the second consecutive year, leading ABC News to eight total wins at the 47th annual News Emmy Awards.

National Geographic earned seven News Emmy awards, driven by wins for Trafficked With Mariana van Zeller. The strong showing by National Geographic marked a significant presence for the Disney-owned channel at the awards ceremony.

cards.headline: Student Criticizes CBS News Direction While Accepting Mike Wallace Scholarship
cards.teaser: Santiago Campos called out CBS News during his acceptance speech for the Mike Wallace Memorial Scholarship at the News Emmy Awards.
cards.body:
Santiago Campos, a senior from District of Columbia International School in Washington, addressed CBS News directly while accepting the Mike Wallace Memorial Scholarship at the News Emmy Awards. He stated that the recent direction of the outlet stains the legacy of Mike Wallace.

Former CBS Evening News anchor Scott Pelley presented the scholarship, which is named after the legendary CBS journalist. Campos' remarks drew attention from the awards ceremony crowd as he accepted the honor for student journalism.

cards.headline: Steven Spielberg Opposes Using AI for Creative Decisions in Filmmaking
cards.teaser: The director said he supports AI for medical solutions but draws the line at using it for creative processes in Hollywood.
cards.body:
Steven Spielberg spoke against artificial intelligence in filmmaking during an appearance on Michelle Obama and Craig Robinson's IMO podcast. He said he thinks AI can be useful to find solutions to medical issues but opposes its use in creative decision-making.

Spielberg stated that he draws the line at AI being the final word on anything creative in Hollywood. The director's comments address ongoing discussions in the film industry about the role of artificial intelligence in production and creative processes.

cards.headline: Senator Kim responds to criticism over ICE facility protest
cards.teaser: Democratic Senator Andy Kim fired back at Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin after being criticized for attending a detention facility protest.
cards.body:
Democratic Senator Andy Kim of New Jersey pushed back against Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin on Wednesday after Mullin criticized him for attending a protest outside a migrant detention facility. During a Cabinet meeting at the White House, Mullin referenced Kim's complaint about being hit by pepper ball spray at the demonstration.

Kim rejected the characterization that his participation was a personal matter. The dispute underscores broader disagreements between Democratic lawmakers and the administration regarding immigration enforcement and how migrants are detained.

cards.headline: Morris Day Denies Participation in National Mall Freedom 250 Concert
cards.teaser: The singer said reports of his participation in the June concert are rumors, despite being listed as a headliner by organizers.
cards.body:
Morris Day denied what he called rumors that he and the Time will perform at a Freedom 250 concert on the National Mall next month. Organizers had announced him as a headliner for a show scheduled for June 27 as part of a 16-day patriotic fair in Washington.

The event has drawn attention for its lineup, which also includes Martina McBride, Flo Rida, and Vanilla Ice. Day stated it is a no for him regarding the performance, contradicting the official promotional materials listing him among the performers for the celebration of America's 250th birthday.

cards.headline: Jimmy Kimmel Gets Emotional Honoring Adam Carolla at Walk of Fame Ceremony
cards.teaser: The late-night host called Carolla his life partner while speaking at his Hollywood Walk of Fame ceremony.
cards.body:
Jimmy Kimmel became emotional while paying tribute to Adam Carolla at his Hollywood Walk of Fame ceremony on Wednesday. The late-night host called Carolla his "life partner," quipping that if the description sounded romantic, that was intentional.

Kimmel recalled meeting Carolla in 1994 while working on Kevin and Bean, a Los Angeles radio show. The two have maintained their friendship and professional connection throughout their entertainment careers.

The governor of Washington has characterized the disaster as potentially the deadliest industrial tragedy in the state's modern history. Nine additional workers were injured in the incident. Authorities are continuing recovery operations for the missing workers.

cards.headline: DOJ charges Google employee over insider trading on prediction market
cards.teaser: A Google staffer allegedly used insider information to profit $1.2 million on Polymarket.
cards.body:
The Department of Justice has charged a Google engineer with insider trading after he allegedly used confidential information about Google's 2025 Year in Search campaign to place bets on Polymarket, a prediction market platform. The engineer risked over $2.7 million in wagers and made approximately $1.2 million in profits from the trades.

This marks the second known federal criminal case involving insider trading on a prediction market platform. The charges reflect growing government attention to potential securities violations on prediction markets, which have expanded in popularity but remain largely unregulated.

cards.headline: Republicans reconcile with Ken Paxton after contentious Texas Senate primary
cards.teaser: Party leaders are breaking the ice with Paxton following a brutal primary campaign.
cards.body:
Republican leaders are moving to rebuild relationships with Ken Paxton following a bruising Texas Senate primary. The race created significant divisions within the party, but officials are now working to unify behind Paxton as he prepares for the general election matchup.

Democrat James Talarico is pivoting his strategy for the general election, shifting away from his primary message to attack Paxton's past scandals. Political analysts are evaluating whether Democrats can overcome Texas's long history of favoring Republican candidates in statewide races.

hero.headline: Google engineer charged with insider trading after making $1.2 million on Polymarket
hero.body:
Federal prosecutors in New York charged a longtime Google employee with insider trading after he allegedly used confidential company information to make $1.2 million in bets on Polymarket, a prediction market platform.

The engineer worked at Google and allegedly accessed internal data that gave him an advantage when placing bets on the platform. Prosecutors say he violated insider trading laws by using this non-public information for personal financial gain.

Polymarket allows users to bet on the outcomes of future events, from political elections to economic indicators. The platform has grown in popularity as a way to gauge public sentiment on various topics, but it has also attracted scrutiny over potential manipulation and misuse.

The case marks a notable application of insider trading law beyond traditional stock markets. While insider trading typically involves securities like stocks and bonds, prosecutors are applying similar legal principles to prediction markets where information asymmetry can create unfair advantages.

The charges did not specify what type of internal Google data the employee allegedly accessed or how that information translated into profitable bets on Polymarket. The engineer's position at Google and the duration of the alleged trading activity were also not detailed in available information about the charges.

Google has not publicly commented on the charges against its employee. The company maintains strict policies around the use of confidential information and regularly trains employees on legal and ethical obligations regarding proprietary data.

The case could set precedent for how insider trading laws apply to emerging financial platforms and prediction markets. Legal experts have debated whether traditional securities laws should extend to betting platforms, particularly as these markets grow in size and influence.

If convicted, the engineer could face significant fines and potential prison time. Federal insider trading charges typically carry maximum sentences of 20 years in prison, though actual sentences vary widely based on the specifics of each case and cooperation with authorities.

cards.headline: Trump administration in talks to fund US drone companies
cards.teaser: The administration is discussing financial support for domestic drone manufacturers.
cards.body: The Trump administration has entered into discussions about providing funding to US drone companies. The talks represent a potential shift in government support for the domestic drone manufacturing industry.

cards.headline: FIFA investigated over World Cup ticket pricing practices
cards.teaser: New York and New Jersey are examining whether fans were misled about ticket sales and seating.
cards.body:
The attorneys general of New York and New Jersey have launched an investigation into FIFA's ticket sales and pricing practices. The probe was triggered by reports that fans were misled about ticket availability and seat locations for World Cup matches.

FIFA has been ordered to provide explanations regarding its ticketing approach for the 2026 World Cup. The investigation examines whether the organization gave accurate information to ticket purchasers.

cards.headline: Court orders customs chief to address tariff refund compliance
cards.teaser: A judge demanded the official appear at a hearing about efforts to repay $166 billion in illegally imposed tariffs.
cards.body:
A federal court ordered the head of US Customs to appear at a hearing to address compliance with tariff refund requirements. The demand signals judicial concern about the Trump administration's progress in repaying $166 billion owed from tariffs that were ruled illegal.

The court's decision to require personal appearance by the customs chief represents an escalation in oversight of the refund process. The substantial sum stems from tariffs previously determined to have been imposed without proper legal authority.

cards.headline: Ferrari's first electric car faces criticism from investors and analysts
cards.teaser: The new model sparked memes, analyst skepticism, and a stock selloff following its reveal.
cards.body:
Ferrari's new Luce electric vehicle has sparked significant backlash following its unveiling. Social media users mocked the model, while analysts questioned its market viability. The negative reception prompted investors to sell shares in the Italian automaker.

A former Ferrari chairman expressed concerns that the shift to electric vehicles could damage the company's storied legacy. The divided public response highlights challenges Ferrari faces as it navigates the transition away from traditional combustion engines amid competition from Chinese EV makers.

hero.headline: Australia sues 3M for $2 billion over contamination from firefighting foam
hero.teaser: The Australian government has filed a lawsuit against 3M seeking $2 billion in damages over contamination caused by PFAS chemicals.
hero.body:
Australia's government has launched what it calls its largest ever lawsuit, seeking $2 billion in damages from 3M over PFAS contamination at 28 defence bases. The American manufacturing company produced firefighting foam containing PFAS chemicals, known as "forever chemicals" because they persist indefinitely in the environment and human bodies.

The contamination stems from decades of using the foam for firefighting training and emergency response at Australian defence facilities. The government is pursuing the case to recover costs associated with addressing the widespread contamination across the affected sites.

cards.headline: California court rejects Tesla's bid to dismiss racial discrimination lawsuit
cards.teaser: A California court has denied Tesla's attempt to throw out a racial discrimination lawsuit, clearing the way for a trial in July.
cards.body: A California court has rejected Tesla's motion to dismiss a racial discrimination lawsuit before trial. The state's civil rights agency, which brought the case, called the ruling a victory and said it expects to proceed to trial in July. The lawsuit alleges racial discrimination at Tesla facilities, and the agency will now present its case against the electric vehicle manufacturer in court.

cards.headline: Rivian sets June 9 for first R2 SUV deliveries
cards.teaser: Rivian will deliver its first R2 SUVs to customers on June 9, the company announced.
cards.body:
Rivian has announced June 9 as the date for first customer deliveries of the R2 SUV. CEO RJ Scaringe has described the vehicle as "maybe the most important thing we've launched to date," underscoring its significance to the company's future.

The R2 marks an important expansion of Rivian's product lineup beyond its initial R1T truck and R1S SUV models.

cards.headline: NASA spacecraft captures detailed Mars images during flyby
cards.teaser: A NASA spacecraft has sent back high-resolution images of Mars, including views of the south pole, during a recent flyby.
cards.body:
The Psyche spacecraft captured spectacular views of Mars as it passed by the red planet on its journey to study a distant asteroid. The images include high-resolution photographs of the Martian south pole.

The Mars flyby was not Psyche's primary mission objective. Instead, the spacecraft is traveling to examine a metal-rich asteroid in the asteroid belt, making these images a bonus scientific opportunity during its voyage through the inner solar system.

cards.headline: Researchers achieve perfectly random number generation using quantum chips
cards.teaser: Scientists have created certifiably perfect randomness for the first time using entangled quantum computing chips.
cards.body:
The experimental randomness amplification was achieved through quantum entanglement between chips. True randomness has applications in cryptography and data security, where unpredictable numbers are essential for protecting information.

The quantum computing system's ability to generate perfect randomness could help keep secrets safe by making encryption keys impossible to predict. Previous random number generators relied on methods that could theoretically be compromised or predicted with enough computing power.

hero.headline: Hurricanes Take Commanding 3-1 Lead in Eastern Conference Finals
hero.body:
The Carolina Hurricanes moved within one win of reaching the Stanley Cup Final after defeating the Montreal Canadiens in Game 4 of the Eastern Conference finals. Goaltender Frederik Andersen recorded a shutout with 18 saves, his third of the postseason through 12 playoff games this year.

The Hurricanes dominated in Montreal, building a 3-1 series lead over the Canadiens. Andersen turned away every shot he faced to secure the victory on the road. The win puts Carolina in position to close out the series in Game 5, scheduled for Friday.

The shutout performance marked Andersen's third clean sheet of these playoffs, demonstrating the veteran goaltender's consistency in high-pressure situations. His 18-save night was part of a comprehensive team effort that saw the Hurricanes control play throughout the game.

Carolina now has three opportunities to advance to the Stanley Cup Final, starting with Game 5. The Hurricanes have outscored and outplayed Montreal through four games of the series, establishing themselves as the clear favorites to represent the Eastern Conference in the championship round.

The Canadiens face elimination as they prepare to host Game 5 on Friday. Montreal will need to win three consecutive games to overturn the series deficit and advance to the Final. The team has struggled to generate offense against Andersen and the Hurricanes' defensive structure throughout the conference finals.

If Carolina completes the series win, they will await the winner of the Western Conference finals for a chance at the franchise's second Stanley Cup championship. The Hurricanes' playoff run has been built on strong goaltending and balanced scoring, elements that were on full display in their Game 4 victory.

cards.headline: SEC Commissioner Defends Conference Despite Big Ten Playoff Dominance
cards.teaser: Greg Sankey said the SEC still 'stands alone' despite the Big Ten winning the past three national titles and holding a 4-0 record against the SEC in recent College Football Playoff matchups.
cards.body:
SEC Commissioner Greg Sankey declared his conference still stands alone as the nation's best, despite the Big Ten's recent dominance. The Big Ten has won three consecutive national championships and maintains a perfect 4-0 record against the SEC in head-to-head College Football Playoff matchups over the past three seasons.

Despite the stark on-field evidence favoring the Big Ten, Sankey maintained confidence in the SEC's overall strength and continued relevance in college football's power structure.

cards.headline: Georgia Coach Suggests SEC Could Leave NCAA Over Playoff Disagreements
cards.teaser: Kirby Smart commented that the SEC might essentially secede if an agreement cannot be reached on College Football Playoff matters.
cards.body:
Georgia head coach Kirby Smart indicated during college football spring meetings that the SEC could leave the NCAA if no agreement is reached on playoff format issues. His comments about the conference potentially seceding have raised significant questions about the future direction of college football governance.

Conference expansion has been a major focus of the spring meetings. Smart's remarks represent an escalation in ongoing discussions about playoff structures and the SEC's role within the current NCAA framework.

cards.headline: Phillies Pitcher Cristopher Sanchez Sets Franchise Record With Scoreless Streak
cards.teaser: Cristopher Sanchez extended his scoreless innings streak to 44 innings, surpassing a Phillies franchise record set by Hall of Famer Grover Cleveland Alexander in 1911.
cards.body:
Phillies pitcher Cristopher Sánchez set a new franchise record on Wednesday, extending his scoreless innings streak to 44⅔ innings. He surpassed the previous mark held by Hall of Famer Grover Cleveland Alexander, whose record had stood since 1911.

Sánchez's achievement represents the longest scoreless streak in Philadelphia Phillies history, breaking a record that had lasted over a century.

cards.headline: Arizona Forward Koa Peat Stays in NBA Draft
cards.teaser: Koa Peat, a projected first-round pick, is keeping his name in the NBA draft after playing forward for Arizona.
cards.body:
Arizona forward Koa Peat has decided to keep his name in the NBA draft, sources told ESPN on Wednesday. Peat is projected to be selected in the first round.

The decision means the forward will forgo returning to college basketball and instead pursue his professional career in the NBA.

cards.headline: Former Super Bowl MVP Von Miller Lobbies Broncos for Return
cards.teaser: Von Miller said he is playing for somebody in the 2026 season and has already asked Denver coach Sean Payton to sign him.
cards.body:
Former Super Bowl MVP Von Miller has made it clear he will play in the 2026 season. In recent comments, Miller said he is "for sure" suiting up for somebody next year and has already reached out to Denver Broncos head coach Sean Payton about a potential return.

Miller, who previously won a Super Bowl with the Broncos, is lobbying the franchise to bring him back. The overture to Payton represents Miller's direct pitch to reunite with his former team.

hero.headline: Horror Film Obsession Breaks Box Office Record With Second-Weekend Spike
hero.body:
The horror film Obsession has made box office history by increasing its earnings in its second weekend, a pattern not seen since Sound of Freedom. The film has become what industry observers are calling this summer's breakout box office hit.

The second-weekend spike marks an unusual achievement in theatrical releases, where films typically see declining revenues after their opening weekend. The performance has drawn comparisons to Sound of Freedom, which similarly saw audience growth after its initial release.

Industry tracking shows the film's momentum continuing beyond typical horror movie patterns. The success has established Obsession as a record-breaking entry in the horror genre, though specific box office figures were not disclosed in initial reports.

The film's photography has also drawn attention from industry publications, with critics highlighting its visual approach. The combination of strong word-of-mouth and repeat viewings appears to be driving the continued box office performance.

Obsession's trajectory differs from standard horror releases, which often front-load their earnings during opening weekend before sharp declines. The sustained audience interest suggests the film is reaching beyond typical horror demographics.

The achievement comes during a competitive summer movie season. While many releases see diminishing returns after their debuts, Obsession has bucked industry trends with measurable growth in its second frame.

Distribution analysts are watching whether the film can maintain momentum into subsequent weekends. The second-weekend increase has already secured its place in box office history, joining Sound of Freedom as one of the rare films to achieve this pattern in recent years.

The success represents a significant win for the horror genre, which has produced several breakout hits in recent years but rarely with this specific pattern of sustained growth after opening weekend.

cards.headline: ABC News and National Geographic Win Big at News Emmy Awards
cards.teaser: ABC News took eight awards including the top prize for outstanding live news program at the 47th annual News Emmys.
cards.body:
ABC World News Tonight With David Muir won the outstanding live news program category for the second consecutive year, leading ABC News to eight total wins at the 47th annual News Emmy Awards.

National Geographic earned seven News Emmy awards, driven by wins for Trafficked With Mariana van Zeller. The strong showing by National Geographic marked a significant presence for the Disney-owned channel at the awards ceremony.

cards.headline: Student Criticizes CBS News Direction While Accepting Mike Wallace Scholarship
cards.teaser: Santiago Campos called out CBS News during his acceptance speech for the Mike Wallace Memorial Scholarship at the News Emmy Awards.
cards.body:
Santiago Campos, a senior from District of Columbia International School in Washington, addressed CBS News directly while accepting the Mike Wallace Memorial Scholarship at the News Emmy Awards. He stated that the recent direction of the outlet stains the legacy of Mike Wallace.

Former CBS Evening News anchor Scott Pelley presented the scholarship, which is named after the legendary CBS journalist. Campos' remarks drew attention from the awards ceremony crowd as he accepted the honor for student journalism.

cards.headline: Steven Spielberg Opposes Using AI for Creative Decisions in Filmmaking
cards.teaser: The director said he supports AI for medical solutions but draws the line at using it for creative processes in Hollywood.
cards.body:
Steven Spielberg spoke against artificial intelligence in filmmaking during an appearance on Michelle Obama and Craig Robinson's IMO podcast. He said he thinks AI can be useful to find solutions to medical issues but opposes its use in creative decision-making.

Spielberg stated that he draws the line at AI being the final word on anything creative in Hollywood. The director's comments address ongoing discussions in the film industry about the role of artificial intelligence in production and creative processes.

cards.headline: Morris Day Denies Participation in National Mall Freedom 250 Concert
cards.teaser: The singer said reports of his participation in the June concert are rumors, despite being listed as a headliner by organizers.
cards.body:
Morris Day denied what he called rumors that he and the Time will perform at a Freedom 250 concert on the National Mall next month. Organizers had announced him as a headliner for a show scheduled for June 27 as part of a 16-day patriotic fair in Washington.

The event has drawn attention for its lineup, which also includes Martina McBride, Flo Rida, and Vanilla Ice. Day stated it is a no for him regarding the performance, contradicting the official promotional materials listing him among the performers for the celebration of America's 250th birthday.

cards.headline: Jimmy Kimmel Gets Emotional Honoring Adam Carolla at Walk of Fame Ceremony
cards.teaser: The late-night host called Carolla his life partner while speaking at his Hollywood Walk of Fame ceremony.
cards.body:
Jimmy Kimmel became emotional while paying tribute to Adam Carolla at his Hollywood Walk of Fame ceremony on Wednesday. The late-night host called Carolla his "life partner," quipping that if the description sounded romantic, that was intentional.

Kimmel recalled meeting Carolla in 1994 while working on Kevin and Bean, a Los Angeles radio show. The two have maintained their friendship and professional connection throughout their entertainment careers.

hero.headline: US military strikes Iranian drone site amid ongoing peace negotiations
hero.body:
The US military shot down four Iranian attack drones and struck a ground control station in Bandar Abbas that was preparing to launch a fifth drone, a US official said Wednesday. The incident occurred in the Strait of Hormuz when Iranian forces targeted a commercial ship with one-way attack drones.

US Central Command confirmed its forces intercepted the drones that posed a threat in the strait. Bandar Abbas is a port city on Iran's southern coast. A senior US official characterized this as the second such clash in 48 hours.

The military action took place as the US and Iran are engaged in negotiations to end their ongoing conflict. President Donald Trump addressed the situation during a Cabinet meeting Wednesday, though his remarks differed from weekend statements suggesting an agreement was near. Trump maintained what officials described as maximum demands on Iran during the talks.

The strikes represent a continuation of military tensions even as diplomatic efforts proceed. The US attacked the Iranian drone-launching unit on the ground before it could deploy additional weapons, according to the senior official who spoke on condition of anonymity.

The Strait of Hormuz serves as a critical waterway for global shipping and energy transport. Iranian drone attacks on commercial vessels in the area have occurred repeatedly during the broader conflict between the two nations. US forces maintain a regular presence in the region to protect shipping lanes and respond to threats against civilian maritime traffic.

Neither government has provided details about the substance of ongoing peace negotiations or a timeline for potential agreement. The continued military exchanges raise questions about the progress of diplomatic talks aimed at resolving the conflict.

cards.headline: Justice Department opens investigation into Trump accuser E. Jean Carroll
cards.teaser: The DOJ has launched a criminal investigation into E. Jean Carroll focusing on possible perjury in her deposition testimony.
cards.body:
The Trump administration has opened a criminal investigation into E. Jean Carroll, the writer who accused President Trump of sexual assault. According to reports from CNN and the New York Times, prosecutors are examining whether Carroll committed perjury during a 2022 deposition tied to her civil lawsuits against Trump.

The investigation focuses on statements Carroll made under oath about whether she received outside financial support for her legal battles. Carroll previously won civil verdicts against Trump in cases involving defamation and sexual assault allegations.

cards.headline: Former judges ask court to reopen Trump IRS settlement case
cards.teaser: A bipartisan group of former federal judges challenged the Trump administration's settlement that created a $1.776 billion fund.
cards.body:
A group of former federal judges asked a federal court Wednesday to reopen President Trump's lawsuit against the Internal Revenue Service. The judges argued that the administration circumvented the court by negotiating a settlement with the president directly.

The settlement created a $1.776 billion fund for people who believe the government has wronged them. The bipartisan group of former judges contends this arrangement bypassed proper judicial oversight of the case.

cards.headline: Appeals court allows Palestinian activist to remain free pending Supreme Court appeal
cards.teaser: A federal appeals panel ruled that Mahmoud Khalil can stay out of custody while petitioning the Supreme Court.
cards.body:
A federal appeals court panel ruled Tuesday that pro-Palestinian activist Mahmoud Khalil may remain free while he appeals his case against the Trump administration to the Supreme Court. The three-judge panel included judges appointed by Presidents Trump, George W. Bush, and Joe Biden.

Judges Stephanos Bibas, Arianna Freeman, and Thomas Hardiman issued the decision, allowing Khalil to proceed with his legal challenge while the case moves forward in the Supreme Court.

cards.headline: Senator Kim responds to criticism over ICE facility protest
cards.teaser: Democratic Senator Andy Kim fired back at Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin after being criticized for attending a detention facility protest.
cards.body:
Democratic Senator Andy Kim of New Jersey pushed back against Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin on Wednesday after Mullin criticized him for attending a protest outside a migrant detention facility. During a Cabinet meeting at the White House, Mullin referenced Kim's complaint about being hit by pepper ball spray at the demonstration.

Kim rejected the characterization that his participation was a personal matter. The dispute underscores broader disagreements between Democratic lawmakers and the administration regarding immigration enforcement and how migrants are detained.
